@FeatureCell

The @FeatureCell decorator is an Angular-only API that marks an injectable class as a FeatureCell within the SDuX Vault. It establishes FeatureCell identity, state typing, and vault integration using Angular’s dependency injection model.

Decorator Contract Summary

  • Declares a class as a FeatureCell provider
  • Assigns a unique FeatureCell key
  • Anchors the FeatureCell’s state type at compile time
  • Enables typed vault injection via injectVault<T>()
  • Integrates with Angular DI and lifecycle management

The @FeatureCell decorator defines identity and typing only. It does not execute pipelines, initialize the FeatureCell, or emit state. Its responsibility is limited to attaching stable metadata that the Vault orchestrator reads during Angular-based registration.

Note

This decorator is available only when using /angular. Non-Angular environments must use provideFeatureCell() for FeatureCell registration.

Purpose

In Angular applications, FeatureCells are typically implemented as injectable services. The @FeatureCell decorator bridges the gap between Angular’s DI system and the Vault runtime by attaching FeatureCell metadata directly to the class constructor.

This metadata allows the Vault to:

  • Register the FeatureCell under a stable, unique key
  • Infer the FeatureCell’s state type everywhere it is consumed
  • Provide strongly typed vault instances through dependency injection

Unlike framework decorators, @FeatureCell does not rely on reflection or runtime type analysis. It stores explicit metadata using stable keys that are read by the Vault orchestrator during registration.

Decorator Signature
FeatureCell<TState>
Signature Description
@FeatureCell<TState>

inputs:

  • key: string
 Declares the decorated class as a FeatureCell and assigns it a unique key. The generic type parameter TState defines the strongly typed state managed by the FeatureCell.
State Typing

The generic type parameter supplied to @FeatureCell<TState> establishes the authoritative state type for the FeatureCell. This type is captured at compile time and propagated throughout the system.

This enables:

  • Strong typing for injectVault<TState>()
  • Type-safe reducers, filters, interceptors, and merges
  • Consistent state typing across services, components, and controllers

The decorator internally stores a type anchor to preserve the generic state type without introducing runtime overhead. This mechanism exists solely to support TypeScript inference and does not affect execution.

Usage

A FeatureCell is typically declared as an Angular service. The @FeatureCell decorator is applied alongside @Injectable(), and the vault is injected using injectVault<T>().

Example: Declaring an Angular FeatureCell

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService,
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: [] 
      }
    )
  ]
};
          
// bank-employee.service.ts
// The provideFeatureCell key must match the @FeatureCell key input
          
import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { FeatureCell, injectVault } from '@sdux-vault/angular';
import { Employee } from './employee.shape';

@FeatureCell`}}<BankEmployeeShape>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Required to activate the FeatureCell
    this.vault.initialize();
  }
}`}}

What this does

  • Declares the service as a FeatureCell
  • Registers the FeatureCell under a unique key
  • Establishes strongly typed state for the cell
  • Integrates the FeatureCell with Angular DI
  • Requires explicit initialization to become operable
Rules & Constraints
  • Defines FeatureCell identity
    The @FeatureCell decorator declares the unique key and state type used to create the FeatureCell’s Angular DI token.
  • FeatureCell keys must be globally unique
    Each FeatureCell key may be registered only once within the application. Duplicate keys result in a runtime error outside of DevMode.
  • Creation occurs during registration
    The FeatureCell token is created when provideFeatureCell() is evaluated, not when the service is instantiated.
  • DevMode relaxes enforcement for testing
    In DevMode, duplicate keys may be tolerated to support hot reloads and isolated test environments. Production builds enforce strict uniqueness.

These constraints ensure that each FeatureCell has a single, unambiguous owner within the Angular dependency graph and that state boundaries remain deterministic.

Initialization

Applying @FeatureCell does not initialize the FeatureCell. Initialization is a required, explicit step that activates the pipeline, behaviors, and state emission.

If initialize() is not called, the FeatureCell is considered inactive and any attempt to use state APIs will result in a runtime error.

Initialization is typically performed in the service constructor, but may be deferred if advanced lifecycle control is required.
